notes: Shared tile catalogue for map files (the project's maps/*.json). Maps are independent of any combat type: a combat mode reads these properties and decides what they mean for its rules.

symbol: the character a tile is saved as in a map file's rows. Unknown symbols load as floor. Only ' is left of the printable ASCII characters (" and \ are avoided), so later tiles use single Latin-1 letters (À onward, skipping × and ÷); then Latin Extended-A from Ā; next free: ē.
solid: blocks movement. blocksSight: blocks line of sight. cover: standing next to it can give cover. height: block height in pixels (0 = floor tile).

fade: drawn see-through while it hides a party member standing behind it (exploration and Combat Type 1; the map editor's Fade checkbox edits it). wall: drawn wallHeightScale times as tall in exploration and Combat Type 1, always full height there (no heightVariants), since fading keeps the party visible. Designer decision (Oct 2026): walls 2x, walls fade by default.

panels: a built wall (not rock, ice, cliffs or hive) that, in exploration and Combat Type 1, is drawn in two-tile panels: two of the same wall side by side in a straight run read as one panel, and every other panel along a run has a window (maps/wallPanels.js). Presentation only: windows don't change sight. Designer decision (Oct 2026). windowView 'space': the windows show a star field (starship and alien vessel bulkheads).

tall: a large object (trees, spires, pillars, silos, masts) drawn wallHeightScale times as tall in exploration and Combat Type 1, like walls. big: in those views, a 2x2 square of the same object is drawn as one object twice the size (2x2 and 2x high: a big boulder, a giant tree); objects left over stay single (maps/bigObjects.js). Tall and big objects fade, except objects 32 high or lower (boulders, ice blocks, ore veins, cacti, fountains, fuel tanks, parked shuttles; designer decision Oct 2026). Presentation only: movement, sight and cover still read the single tiles. Designer request (Oct 2026): 'large objects such as trees should be 2x high... some boulders or large land features 2x or 2x2'; which tiles are tall or big is a prototype proposal.
role: 'hazard' (a floor tile a hazardControl can make dangerous) or 'hazardControl' (the interactable that sets it off); null for none.

Images are 64 x 96 PNGs with the tile's 64 x 32 floor diamond across the bottom (generated by scripts/makeTiles.mjs). heightVariants: lower versions of a wall (bulkhead, rock wall, prefab wall) used on the front edge and inside the map so walls don't hide the room. Outdoor, cave, city and wreck tiles are prototype placeholders for Generate Map's layout types. Deep water, lava and crevasses are flat but impassable (solid, height 0) and don't block sight. activeImage: drawn over the tile while it is active (live hazard, console light).

Starship wall fittings (lcarsWall, conduitWall, hatchWall, computerWall): bulkheads with an LCARS display, EPS conduit, Jefferies tube hatch or computer bank, placed by hand in the editor. Their art is the v2 sample art (public/art/tiles-v2/, scripts/makeTilesV2.mjs) whichever tile art is chosen; their lower versions are the plain bulkhead's. They don't pair into window panels. lights: animated light-only overlays (image, style: pulse, blink or flicker) drawn over the tile. Presentation only.

panelFitting (lcarsPanel, conduitPanel, hatchPanel, computerPanel): the long versions of the wall fittings, a plain bulkhead with panels whose every two-tile panel shows the fitting (lcars, conduit, hatch or computer, drawn by IsoTiles.jsx FittingHalf) instead of a window. The editor lays both tiles at once. Designer request (Oct 2026).

Walls for the locations and biomes that had none (breachedBulkhead to obsidianWall) and the Derelict Ship and Detention Block floors (derelictDeck, cellFloor) are prototype placeholders added on designer request (Oct 2026); their names, heights and looks are a prototype proposal. Map rotation: see maps/mapFormat.js rotated.

Bridge (TOS) tiles (tosDeck to tosVoid): a TOS-inspired starship bridge (station walls with framed displays, main viewscreen, turbolift doors, command well, captain's chair, helm, stations, red railing), art by scripts/makeTilesBridge.mjs. Added on designer request (Oct 2026); the tile list, names, heights and looks are a prototype proposal. The station walls don't pair into window panels. Station consoles and the helm run the length of their tile, so a row of them reads as one console. tosHull: the plain outside of the ring, for the near walls (which show their outer faces). tosVoid: empty space outside the room (a transparent, impassable floor). joinImages: in the editor, exploration and Combat Type 1 a railing is drawn as the piece joining it to up to two neighbouring railings ({joins} = their directions, e.g. N-SE; maps/railJoins.js), so curved runs read as one railing; Combat Type 2 draws the plain tile.

paletteGroups: the map editor's collapsible tile categories, in order, by what each tile was made for. section: the heading the category sits under (Locations, Alien Locations, Earth-like Biomes, Alien Biomes). A tile listed in no group shows under Other.
